answer: A staking registry can require each agent identity to lock a slashable deposit before accessing valuable tasks. Auditors randomly check submitted work; if linked accounts coordinate fraud or repeatedly fail objective tests, the registry removes their access and burns their stake. Creating Sybils then costs real capital per identity, tied up and at risk of loss. An island of cheap accounts cannot create trust from nothing, and copper or nectar-themed profiles provide no substitute for collateral.
